subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Transmission
description: Learn The Transmission in one minute.

hook.text: An engine spins fast but wheels need to turn slow with lots of force. Something has to translate.

buildup.text: That's the transmission—a set of gears that converts engine speed into wheel speed at different ratios.

discovery.text: Low gears multiply torque for starting and climbing. High gears let the engine cruise at low RPM.

twist.text: Without a transmission, you'd need an impossibly large engine just to merge onto a highway.

climax.text: Modern automatics have 8 to 10 gears, constantly picking the perfect ratio for you.

punchline.text: Gears are the translator between engine and road.

quiz.question: Why do cars need multiple gears?
options: To match engine speed to wheel needs

details.summary: The transmission matches engine speed to wheel speed by selecting different gear ratios, allowing the engine to operate in its efficient power band at any vehicle speed from crawling to highway cruising.
details.whyItMatters: Without a transmission, an engine could only provide useful power over a narrow speed range. Gear ratios let a single engine handle everything from steep hill climbs to high-speed cruising.
takeaways: Lower gears multiply torque for acceleration and hill climbing
Higher gears reduce RPM for quiet, efficient highway cruising
Modern transmissions may have 8, 9, or even 10 forward gears

faq.question: What is a CVT and why do some people dislike it?
faq.answer: A continuously variable transmission uses a belt and pulleys instead of fixed gears, offering infinite ratios. Some drivers dislike the droning engine sound at constant RPM, but CVTs maximize fuel efficiency.

faq.question: Do electric cars have transmissions?
faq.answer: Most EVs use a single-speed reduction gear because electric motors produce useful torque across such a wide RPM range that multiple gears are unnecessary. Porsche's Taycan is a rare exception with two speeds.
